Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.

title: Value Strategist
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

ElevenLabs is looking for a Value Strategist to help our customers identify, quantify, and realize the business value of ElevenLabs across our portfolio, with a primary focus on ElevenAgents.

This is a senior individual contributor role within our global Revenue organization, spanning the full customer lifecycle from early sales conversations through proof of concept, deployment, renewal, and expansion. You will work directly with customers and prospects to understand their businesses, build the case for investment, and establish how that value will be measured over time.

On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. We are looking for a builder and a doer: someone who can engage credibly with senior customer stakeholders, get deep into a customer's operations and data, build rigorous models themselves, and turn ambiguous business problems into clear, actionable recommendations.

You will define how ElevenLabs understands, measures, and communicates customer value globally.

In this role you will

  • Shape value from the beginning. Partner with Revenue teams and prospects early in the sales cycle to understand customer priorities, identify high-value opportunities, and establish the business case for investing in ElevenLabs.

  • Build our global value strategy. Develop the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, discovery approaches, and playbooks that define how ElevenLabs approaches value across industries and use cases.

  • Scale what works. Turn bespoke work with our largest customers into repeatable approaches that enable our Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial teams to articulate and measure value without requiring bespoke support for every customer.

  • Identify where ElevenLabs can have the greatest impact. Develop a deep understanding of a customer's business, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities to determine which use cases have the greatest potential and why.

  • Quantify the opportunity. Build rigorous financial and operational models that translate ElevenLabs use cases into measurable outcomes across revenue, cost, productivity, customer experience, and other relevant dimensions.

  • Define how value will be proven. Establish success metrics and measurement approaches for proofs of concept and deployments so that customers and ElevenLabs have a shared understanding of what success looks like from the outset.

  • Measure value realization. Partner with customers and internal teams after deployment to understand the impact ElevenLabs is delivering, identify gaps between expected and realized value, and determine where additional opportunities exist.

  • Support expansion and long-term customer value. Use insights from existing deployments to help customers understand what they have achieved and identify where ElevenLabs can drive additional impact.

  • Work directly with the data. Analyze customer and industry data, build models, pressure-test assumptions, and develop recommendations yourself. You should be equally comfortable working in the details and communicating the implications.

  • Partner with Deployment. On strategic accounts, work alongside Deployment Strategists who own the account-level business case, contributing methodology and capturing what works into reusable assets. Across the rest of the book, be the primary owner of value quantification and measurement.

  • Influence senior stakeholders. Communicate complex analysis simply and credibly, and engage with senior leaders internally and externally when the opportunity requires it.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of relevant experience across operating roles, strategy, management consulting, analytics, finance, customer strategy, or other roles requiring rigorous business problem solving.

  • Strong operating judgment. You understand how businesses work and can quickly get underneath a customer's operating model, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities.

  • Exceptional analytical ability. You can personally build sophisticated financial and operational models, work with incomplete or imperfect information, make assumptions explicit, and turn analysis into decisions.

  • Structured problem solving. You are comfortable starting with an ambiguous question such as "Where could AI create the most value in this business?" and developing a rigorous approach to answering it.

  • Customer credibility. You can work directly with customers across functions and levels, ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and establish trust quickly.

  • Commercial judgment. You understand how business value connects to technology investment decisions and can partner closely with Revenue teams while maintaining an objective, customer-first perspective.

  • Excellent communication. You can distill complex analysis into a clear point of view and communicate it effectively in writing and verbally, from working teams through senior executives.

  • A builder mentality. You are excited to start by doing the work yourself, learn from customers, and turn what works into scalable methodologies and tools.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and pace. You can move quickly across industries, customer types, and use cases while maintaining a high bar for analytical rigor.

  • Ability to operate globally. You are comfortable partnering with teams and customers across regions and traveling when valuable for customer work.

  • Willingness to travel. Must be willing and able to travel up to 10% of the time.

Bonus points

  • Experience in strategy or management consulting, particularly in operational transformation, technology, customer experience, or growth.

  • Experience as an operator within a technology company or other fast-moving business.

  • Experience working on AI, automation, customer experience, or technology-enabled business transformation.

  • Experience developing business cases, value frameworks, or analytical methodologies that were ultimately scaled beyond an individual project or customer.

  • Experience working with enterprise customers on complex, cross-functional initiatives.

Location

This is a global role within the Revenue organization. The role can be based in San Francisco or remotely, with the option to work from our San Francisco office.

You will work with customers and ElevenLabs teams across regions and should expect travel for customer meetings and onsite work when it meaningfully advances the work.

Dans le cadre du développement de notre centre technique en Suisse, nous recherchons un(e) Technicien(ne) en robotique – Maintenance & SAV.

Vous assurez le diagnostic, la réparation, la maintenance, la configuration et la mise en service de robots professionnels de nettoyage.

  • Électronique & électricité : batteries, cartes électroniques, moteurs, capteurs, LiDAR, câblages

Nous recherchons une personne technique, polyvalente, curieuse et orientée solutions, qui aime comprendre le fonctionnement d’une machine et rechercher l’origine d’une panne.

  • Automaticien(ne) CFC

  • Très bonne aisance informatique

  • Autonomie, rigueur et sens pratique

description:

Our Operating Principles

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

 

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

 

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

 

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

 

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

 

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

title: Head of Product (m/w/d)
description:
Über DrAnsay

DrAnsay wurde 2018 gegründet und gehört heute zu den führenden digitalen Gesundheitsplattformen in Deutschland. Als digitales HealthTech-Unternehmen verbinden wir Patient:innen, Ärzt:innen und Apotheken und entwickeln technologische Lösungen, die Gesundheitsversorgung einfacher, schneller und zugänglicher machen. Mehr als 1 Million Patient:innen nutzen unsere Plattform bereits. Unser Anspruch ist klar: digitale Medizin so zu gestalten, dass sie im Alltag wirklich funktioniert.

Wir arbeiten schnell, direkt und mit viel Eigenverantwortung. Wer zu uns kommt, übernimmt nicht einfach nur eine bestehende Rolle, sondern gestaltet Strukturen, Prozesse und Entscheidungen aktiv mit.

Warum es diese Rolle gibt

DrAnsay befindet sich in einer Scale-up-Phase: Die Grundstrukturen der Produktorganisation stehen. Der Fokus liegt jetzt auf Optimierung, Effizienz und der Weiterentwicklung bestehender sowie neuer Produktinitiativen. Unser CPO verantwortet gleichzeitig kommerzielle und strategische Themen der Unternehmensführung. Neue Initiativen brauchen deshalb eine Person, die produktübergreifend Struktur schafft und den Takt hält.

Die Position wird neu geschaffen, um diese Lücke zu schließen. Das ist keine Rolle, in der du Grundlagen aufräumst. Es geht darum, dass wir neue Produkte schneller starten und bei bestehenden Produkten an den richtigen Dingen arbeiten.

Deine Rolle

Als Head of Product übernimmst du die Koordination produktübergreifender Roadmaps und OKR-Zyklen, verantwortest das unternehmensweite Produkt-Reporting und sorgst dafür, dass Metriken, Feature-Impact und Produktstrategie intern klar kommuniziert werden. Du berichtest direkt an unseren CPO und bist Schnittstelle zu einem neunköpfigen Produktteam aus Senior Product Managern und einem UX-Team sowie zu Data, Marketing und Engineering.

Dein Ziel in den ersten Monaten ist es, alle Produktbereiche, unseren Markt und das Team gründlich zu verstehen. Du erkennst, wo Planung, Zusammenarbeit und Dokumentation besser werden können, machst einen Plan und setzt ihn um.

Was du konkret machst

  • Produktübergreifende Roadmaps über mehrere Produktlinien und Teams hinweg koordinieren, aktuell halten und Abhängigkeiten zwischen Teams früh erkennen und auflösen

  • OKRs und Key Results auf Team-Ebene mit der übergeordneten Produktstrategie verknüpfen und die Zyklen von der Planung bis zur Auswertung begleiten

  • Die Produkt-Metriken und das unternehmensweite Reporting zum Feature-Impact verantworten, gemeinsam mit unserem Data-Team

  • Vorhaben hinterfragen, die zu wenig Kunden- oder Geschäftswert schaffen, und Alternativen vorschlagen

  • User Research strukturiert in laufende Produktentwicklung einbinden, gemeinsam mit unserem Head of UX und dem UX-Team

  • Die Arbeitsweise unserer Product Manager weiterentwickeln, besonders Planung, Dokumentation und Reporting

  • Product Discovery und die frühe Teamstrukturierung neuer Produktinitiativen unterstützen, inklusive Abstimmung mit Engineering

  • Die unternehmensweite Kommunikation zur Produktstrategie aufbauen und Produktentscheidungen für alle nachvollziehbar dokumentieren


Das brauchst du

  • Erfahrung in einer Product-Leadership-Rolle, etwa als Head of Product, Product Lead oder Group Product Manager. Du hast über dein eigenes Produkt hinaus Verantwortung getragen, für mehrere Product Manager, Teams oder Produktbereiche, fachlich oder disziplinarisch

  • Erfahrung mit digitalen Produkten für Endkund:innen (B2C) in einem schnell wachsenden Unternehmen

  • Praxis mit OKRs und Roadmapping: Du hast OKR-Zyklen produktübergreifend koordiniert und Roadmaps für mehrere Teams gepflegt und kommuniziert

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Produktkennzahlen: Du hast Metriken definiert, Feature-Impact gemessen und Reporting für interne Stakeholder aufgebaut

  • Du überzeugst über Argumente und Zahlen, nicht über deine Position, und diskutierst auch mit erfahrenen Product Managern auf Augenhöhe

  • Die Bereitschaft, auch die Strukturarbeit selbst zu machen: Roadmaps pflegen, Updates einfordern, Reporting am Laufen halten

  • Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse (mindestens C1), weil du täglich in beiden Sprachen mit Product, Engineering und Leadership arbeitest

  • Du kannst die Tätigkeit dauerhaft aus Deutschland ausüben und verfügst zum Start über die hierfür erforderliche Arbeitserlaubnis

Das fällt positiv auf

  • Erfahrung als Head of Product. Voraussetzung ist sie nicht

  • Mehrjährige eigene Produktverantwortung als Product Manager, bevor du in eine Leadership-Rolle gewechselt bist

  • Erfahrung aus einer größeren Produktorganisation mit ausgereiften Arbeitsweisen

  • Erfahrung mit Roadmap- und Produktmanagement-Tools wie airfocus, Productboard, Jira Product Discovery oder Aha!

  • Erfahrung mit Produktanalyse-Tools wie PostHog, Amplitude oder Mixpanel

  • Produkterfahrung in E-Commerce, Marktplätzen oder Digital Health

  • Erfahrung in stark regulierten Produktumfeldern

  • Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit UX-Teams und der Einbindung von User Research

Was wir bieten

  • Vollzeit und unbefristet, Start ab November 2026

  • 100% Remote: Du arbeitest aus Deutschland, Vollzeit, ohne Standortbindung

  • Eine Rolle, die mitwächst: Je tiefer dein Verständnis von Produkten, Markt und Team, desto mehr Entscheidungen übernimmst du

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit unserem CPO und Zeit, alle Produktbereiche gründlich kennenzulernen

  • Sichtbare Wirkung: Du prägst, wie DrAnsay neue Produkte startet und woran das Product-Team arbeitet

  • Kleines Team mit kurzen Wegen, Low-Ego-Kultur und direktem Feedback

  • Ein Produkt mit realem Nutzen: Wir helfen täglich Menschen, Gesundheitsversorgung einfacher zu bekommen

Wie du dich bewirbst

Bewirb dich direkt über das Bewerbungsformular. Kein Anschreiben erforderlich, wir stellen dir einige kurze Fragen, die uns helfen zu verstehen, wie du arbeitest. Diese Antworten sind uns wichtiger als dein LinkedIn-Profil.

Du hörst von uns innerhalb von fünf Arbeitstagen.

DrAnsay ist ein chancengleicher Arbeitgeber. Bewerbungen werden auf Basis von Qualifikationen und Berufserfahrung bewertet. Alle Bewerbenden werden unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, Herkunft, Behinderung, Religion oder anderen geschützten Merkmalen berücksichtigt. DrAnsay verarbeitet die mit deiner Bewerbung übermittelten personenbezogenen Daten zur Durchführung des Recruitingprozesses.

Du hast bereits Verantwortung in Produktion, Industrie, Logistik oder einem vergleichbaren operativen Umfeld übernommen und möchtest Teams nicht nur verwalten, sondern aktiv weiterentwickeln?

  • Du steuerst Personal-, Einsatz- und Kapazitätsplanung und stellst eine verlässliche Projektbesetzung sicher.

  • Du entwickelst dein Team fachlich und organisatorisch weiter und führst neue Mitarbeitende strukturiert ein.

  • Du stellst eine klare Kommunikation zwischen Mitarbeitenden, Kundenansprechpartnern und Geschäftsführung sicher.

  • Du reagierst souverän auf Abweichungen, Engpässe und kurzfristige operative Herausforderungen.

  • Du dokumentierst Leistungen, Entwicklungen und relevante Abweichungen nachvollziehbar.

  • Du bist regelmäßig auf der Fläche präsent und gehst als Führungskraft voran.

DAS BRINGST DU MIT

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung in einer Führungsfunktion in Produktion, Industrie, Metallverarbeitung, Gießerei, Logistik oder einem vergleichbaren Umfeld.

  • Erfahrung als Produktionsleiter, Projektleiter, Teamleiter, Lagerleiter, Schichtleiter, Vorarbeiter oder Gruppenleiter.

  • Gute Kenntnisse in der Steuerung von Produktionsabläufen, Personalplanung und operativen Kennzahlen.

  • Ein gutes Gespür für Menschen sowie die Fähigkeit, Teams verbindlich, fair und klar zu führen.

  • Eine strukturierte, pragmatische und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise.

  • Durchsetzungsstärke, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und eine ausgeprägte Hands-on-Mentalität.

  • Kommunikationsstärke im Kontakt mit Kunden, Mitarbeitenden und internen Schnittstellen.

  • Führerschein Klasse B.

  • Projektbezogene Reisebereitschaft.

WARUM DIESE POSITION?

Diese Rolle ist für Menschen, die operative Führung ernst nehmen. Du gestaltest nicht aus der Distanz, sondern direkt dort, wo Leistung entsteht.

Du hast sichtbaren Einfluss auf Abläufe, Qualität, Produktivität und die Entwicklung deines Teams. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du eng mit unseren Kunden und der Geschäftsführung zusammen und kannst Prozesse aktiv weiterentwickeln.

KLINGT NACH DIR?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung, wenn du die genannten Muss-Kriterien erfüllst und bereit bist, bundesweit Verantwortung in unseren Kundenprojekten zu übernehmen.

Sende deine Bewerbungsunterlagen einfach über unser Bewerbungsformular oder per E-Mail an

Miguel Schäuble
+49 (0)160 902 151 88

Von der Prozessanalyse über die Projektkonzeption bis zur Umsetzung und Begleitung steht das Erreichen der Produktivitätsziele unserer Kunden im Mittelpunkt unseres Handelns.

Mit rund 3.000 Mitarbeitenden an über 30 Standorten unterstützen wir unsere Kunden dabei, Kosten zu senken, ihre Wettbewerbsfähigkeit zu stärken und sich auf ihre Kernkompetenzen zu konzentrieren. Wir hinterfragen Bestehendes, um Prozesse nachhaltig besser zu gestalten – mit Erfahrung, bewährten Methoden, Transparenz und innovativen Lösungen.

Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training. Our customers — in finance, manufacturing, and public administration — need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We’re building that in Heidelberg.

We are hiring a Senior AI Researcher to join our Pre-training team and to advance the architecture and training of our next generation of foundation models. If you are excited about designing inference-efficient architectures, optimising training recipes that scale reliably, and training models on a large scale cluster (thousands of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs), we would love to hear from you.

Team Culture

We foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. About the Role

As a Senior AI Researcher in Pre-training (f/m/d), you will own the critical technical levers that determine the success of our next-generation models: architecture, optimization, stability, and scaling.

Working at the high-leverage intersection of research and engineering, you will translate mathematical reasoning and empirical observations into principled training decisions - from small-scale proxy experiments to multi-thousand-GPU runs.

We are looking for an expert who can combine rigorous experimental design with high-quality production code, directly influencing model quality, run reliability, and the efficiency of the models we ship.

Your Responsibilities

  • Recipe & Architecture Optimization: Own core elements of the training recipe (optimizers, schedules, initialization) and design PyTorch-based architectural improvements to maximize convergence, stability, and training efficiency.

  • Scaling Strategy & Predictability: Develop hyperparameter scaling laws and scale-up methodologies, using small-scale proxy experiments to reliably predict multi-thousand-GPU behavior and de-risk major training decisions.

  • Stability, Diagnostics & Debugging: Investigate complex convergence issues (loss spikes, divergence) and resolve hard-to-reproduce distributed system failures like communication bottlenecks, race conditions, and synchronization errors.

  • System-Model Co-Design: Partner with Compute Performance, Data, Evaluation, and Post-Training teams to align the model lifecycle with hardware constraints, memory bandwidth, and communication topologies.

Core Qualifications

  • You are proficient in Python and deeply familiar with PyTorch-based training workflows.

  • You have a strong track record in machine learning research and software engineering, demonstrated through shipped models, impactful open-source contributions, or published research.

  • You have a strong mathematical foundation and are comfortable reasoning formally about optimisation, scaling behaviour, and training dynamics.

  • You deeply understand transformer training dynamics, optimisation, and the behaviour of large distributed training jobs.

  • You can design rigorous experiments, reason clearly from noisy results, and translate empirical observations into robust training decisions.

  • Hands-on experience pre-training large models (e.g., 7B+ parameters) on substantial infrastructure (e.g., 100+ GPU clusters).

  • You apply strong software engineering practices, including writing maintainable, well-tested code and supporting reproducible experimentation workflows.

  • You are able to implement complex model architectures efficiently and reliably and to debug complex issues across model code, training dynamics, and distributed systems.

  • You collaborate effectively within a research and engineering team and communicate clearly about your work across Pre-training and the broader AAR/AA organization.

  • You are able to work in Germany and collaborate regularly on site in Heidelberg as part of the Pre-training team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Large-Scale Training: Hands-on experience training LLMs or multimodal models on large GPU clusters using distributed frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, torchtitan).

  • Predictive Scaling: Familiarity with scaling laws, hyperparameter transfer, or methods for predicting large-scale training behavior from smaller proxy runs.

  • Stability & Performance: Experience profiling distributed jobs and diagnosing training anomalies like loss spikes, numerical instability, or optimizer pathologies.

  • Advanced Architectures: Exposure to sparse training approaches (e.g., Mixture-of-Experts) and an understanding of their routing and systems trade-offs.

Du sorgst dafür, dass die richtige Botschaft zur richtigen Zeit bei den richtigen Kund:innen ankommt und machst sichtbar, welchen Beitrag CRM zu unserem Wachstum leistet.

entwickelst du CRM bei uns von einem bislang nebenbei betriebenen Kanal zu einer echten Wachstumsfunktion. Die Basis ist da: Klaviyo, mehrere hunderttausend Leads und Kund:innen sowie jede Menge Daten. Was fehlt, ist eine klare CRM-Strategie mit intelligenter Segmentierung, automatisierten Lifecycle-Flows, strukturiertem Testing und einem Reporting, das Wirkung und Umsatzbeitrag sichtbar macht.

Du verschickst bei uns also nicht einfach Newsletter. Du gestaltest, wie wir entlang des gesamten Lifecycles Kund:innen ansprechen und langfristig binden. Dafür bekommst du echte Ownership, viel Gestaltungsspielraum und die Chance, CRM bei Kleines Kraftwerk von Grund auf zu prägen.

Bereit, aus CRM einen echten Wachstumstreiber zu machen?


Wofür du Verantwortung übernimmst



CRM lief bei uns bisher nebenbei – jetzt wollen wir daraus einen echten Wachstumstreiber machen. 

  • Du baust unsere CRM- und Lifecycle-Strategie auf: Du entwickelst Prozesse, Tools und Strukturen von Grund auf und richtest sie auf Kundenbindung und Wiederkäufe aus.
  • Du entwickelst unsere Lifecycle-Flows: In Klaviyo konzipierst und optimierst du automatisierte Customer Journeys von Welcome und Post-Purchase bis Cross-/Upselling und Win-back.
  • Du entwickelst relevante Kundensegmente: Leads und Kund:innen segmentierst du nach Kaufverhalten, Interessen und Lifecycle-Phase für eine gezielte Kundenansprache.

  • Du etablierst eine Test- und Lernkultur: Mit strukturierten A/B-Tests identifizierst du Optimierungspotenziale und entwickelst unsere CRM-Maßnahmen kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Du steuerst die CRM-Performance: Relevante KPIs und Reportings nutzt du, um Erfolge messbar zu machen und konkrete Maßnahmen abzuleiten.
  • Du stellst Datenqualität und Compliance sicher: Du sorgst für sauberes Listenmanagement und DSGVO-konforme CRM-Prozesse.
  • Du identifizierst die größten CRM-Hebel: Potenziale priorisierst du nach Business Impact und entwickelst perspektivisch weitere Retention-Programme wie Loyalty und Referral.


Womit du punkten kannst

Du kennst CRM nicht nur aus der Theorie. Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung im CRM-, Lifecycle- oder Retention-Marketing mit und weißt, wie aus Kundendaten relevante Kommunikation und messbare Kundenbindung entsteht. Dabei wartest du nicht auf Vorgaben, sondern erkennst Potenziale und setzt sie eigenständig um.

  • Du kennst CRM aus der Praxis: Du bringst ca. 4+ Jahre Erfahrung mit, idealerweise im E-Commerce- oder D2C-Umfeld, und hast eine CRM-Funktion bereits aufgebaut oder maßgeblich weiterentwickelt.

  • Du denkst datengetrieben: Du verstehst relevante CRM-KPIs, erkennst Zusammenhänge und leitest daraus konkrete Maßnahmen zur Steigerung von Kundenbindung und Umsatz ab.
  • Du behältst den Überblick und setzt Prioritäten: Kampagnen, Flows, Tests und neue Ideen gleichzeitig bringen dich nicht aus dem Takt. Du entscheidest eigenständig, wo der größte Hebel liegt.
  • Du willst gestalten statt verwalten: Du hast den Anspruch, CRM aktiv aufzubauen, Strukturen zu schaffen und bestehende Ansätze kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.
  • Du kommunizierst souverän: Du arbeitest eng mit unterschiedlichen Teams zusammen und kannst dich auf Deutsch sehr sicher und klar verständigen.

Bewirb dich nicht, wenn …

  • du ein fertiges CRM-Setup mit bestehenden Prozessen und Playbooks übernehmen möchtest – bei uns baust du vieles selbst auf.
  • du lange Freigabeprozesse einer schnellen, direkten Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsführung vorziehst.
  • du ausschließlich Kampagnen versenden möchtest, ohne Verantwortung für Segmentierung, Testing und Reporting zu übernehmen.
  • Datenarbeit für dich eher Pflicht als Werkzeug ist und du ausschließlich kreativ arbeiten möchtest.
  • fehlende Prozesse und Unklarheit dich eher stressen als motivieren – ein fertiges CRM-Handbuch gibt es bei uns noch nicht.


Worauf du dich freuen kannst

  • CRM aufbauen statt nur verwalten: Du bekommst volle Gestaltungsfreiheit beim Aufbau unserer CRM-Funktion und kannst Strukturen, Prozesse und Maßnahmen von Grund auf mitgestalten.

  • Ein Arbeitsplatz zum Wohlfühlen: Dich erwarten moderne, lichtdurchflutete Büros und eine phänomenale Dachterrasse, die zum Durchatmen und Austauschen einlädt.

title: Scientific Product Manager (m/fd)
description:
Your mission

Who we are


NeuroNation is the personalised training app that empowers more than 20 million people all over the world in staying brain healthy and happy in their lives.

We collaborate closely with scientists and universities to achieve the best results possible. Our engaging apps have received awards from major health insurance companies, such as the AOK, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Health. Also, we've been awarded by Apple and Google as one of the best apps available.


To improve the training experience our app provides and make the product more effective and engaging to users and patients, we are looking for a passionate person with a background in science and deep interest in digital health and games. Since the role touches many different fields, you don’t have to bring all know-how already with you - we are welcoming passionate learners who want to develop themselves in this role.


So, if you want to help us shape a better tomorrow, join us on our journey!


Your roles and responsibilities


  • Improve the training experience and the exercises of our mobile and web app by making NeuroNation as effective and engaging as possible
  • Continuously incorporate the latest findings from neuroscience by reading scientific papers and learning from concepts that have been proven to have impact on clinical outcomes
  • Apply User Research and Usability Testing to learn how we can best help users and patients, and define useful features and visual concepts
  • Collaborate with our scientific partners from various universities and clinics to run successful clinical trials with NeuroNation
  • Analyse massive amounts of data continuously collected from millions of users to drive optimal decisions in product development
  • Run A/B tests to experiment with new ideas
  • Be your own user, assure the quality of the product, and become one of the experts for cognitive training
  • Live with a Growth mindset - constantly look for learning opportunities for yourself and the team
  • Work closely with colleagues from Marketing, Business Intelligence, Customer Care, and CRM
  • Join the Growth and Product teams to collaboratively help millions of users and patients to stay fit


Your profile

Who you are and what you have done

  • You have a deep personal interest in BRAIN TRAINING and SELF-IMPROVEMENT
  • You have at least 2 years of working experience in Neuroscience, Cognitive Science, Psychology, or related fields
  • You are a passionate learner
  • You have personal experience as a user of digital health, education, or productivity apps
  • You have personal experience as a user of digital games
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills in both German and English.
  • You have strong problem-solving skills
  • You have a deep interest in analysing engagement, retention, and other behavioural data
  • You are well-organised and have good project management skills. You can multi-task and manage multiple tasks concurrently.
  • You are a team-player and love to help out your colleagues.
  • Bonus: You have experience with Games or Gamification
  • Bonus: You have experience or talent with UX or Visual Design
  • Bonus: You have knowledge of SQL, R, or Python
  • Bonus: You hold a PhD in Neuroscience, Cognitive Science, or Psychology



Why us?

  • Flexible working hours with core hours, so you can balance sport, hobbies, and career
  • A hybrid role in Berlin — 3 days in the office, 2 remote
  • An office at Gendarmenmarkt with events, a roof terrace, snacks, and drinks
  • A bespoke onboarding programme to get you up to speed on the role, products, and teams fast
  • A clear working structure where initiative and creativity are valued
  • Flat hierarchies and an open feedback culture

  • An energetic, motivated, well-organised team
  • Team events and workshops
  • Sponsored gym and sports-class memberships

About Zego 🚀

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

Purpose of the role

As Head of Pricing - Insurance at Zego, you will lead the insurer’s technical view of the models that drive our pricing. That covers the actuarial risk models behind our net rates, the demand and market models, and any other predictive model used for pricing and underwriting decisions. The models are built by the MGA pricing teams using a mix of traditional techniques (GLM, GAM, GBM) as well as new AI driven approaches.

Your role is to make sure that we, as the insurer, can form an actuarial view on all of them, validate what sits underneath, and stand behind the rates it carries. On the actuarial risk models you will go further still, joining those projects from the start and owning the independent validation end to end.

You will do this as the senior technical voice in a small actuarial team, which brings real breadth alongside the depth. Alongside the models you will review pricing and underwriting proposals across both personal and commercial motor in close collaboration with our underwriting team, and you will bring the modelling view into portfolio management.

You will work directly with the MGA pricing teams, with underwriting and with our co-insurance partners, with access to senior leadership and to decision making from the first week.

What you will be working on

  • Lead the insurer’s technical view across the full model landscape: the actuarial risk models, the demand models, the market and optimisation models. For each one the questions are the same: is the approach sound, can the output be trusted, and are we using it the way we intend to.

  • Bring an actuarial view to all modelling approaches including AI driven models. Methods move quickly, you need to keep up.

  • Go deeper on the actuarial risk models that set our net rates: join each project, independently validate the modelling decisions, the rating factor choices and the assumptions applied, and evidence the basis for each.

  • Review, validate and challenge pricing and underwriting proposals across personal and commercial lines, working closely with our underwriting team: tactical pricing changes, full model updates, optimisation algorithms, new underwriting rules and renewal capping.

  • Contribute to portfolio management and portfolio insight: what the KPIs are telling us, what is driving the movements, and what the modelling view says about where performance is heading.

  • Support the insurer’s position with our co-insurance partners on the net rates, the quality of the models behind them and the validation we have carried out.

  • Mentor and coach junior actuarial colleagues.

  • Help build the processes, the governance and the tooling, including AI, that allow a small and senior team to work faster and more robustly.

What you will need to be successful in the role

  • A qualified actuary, or an equivalent track record inside an actuarial pricing team, with at least ten years of hands-on modelling experience.

  • Deep experience of classic actuarial risk modelling: GLMs built in Emblem, Akur8 or equivalent, with Python used in practice rather than in principle.

  • Real exposure to the newer modelling approaches alongside the classic ones, such as GBMs and other machine learning methods, and the confidence to form an actuarial view on a method you have not built yourself.

  • Experience with UK motor pricing. Experience with other lines of business is an advantage.

  • Experience with newly launched portfolios, or portfolios with limited history.

  • Experience with telematics products and their pricing.

  • The judgement to say whether a model can be trusted, backed by having seen models work and seen them fail.

  • Comfort in a small team with high influence and direct access to decision making, and a genuine interest in developing a less experienced colleague.

The Zego ways of working 🏡

Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.

We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It's a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year.

Here is what the last one looked like.

Benefits 🎁

💰 Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year.

🏆 Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution.

📈 Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build

🩺 Private medical insurance.

🏖️ Pension, generous holiday, and £1,000 a year to spend on getting to the office or learning something new.

💻 Cutting-edge systems and tools, so you always have what you need to drive your impact.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? We want to hear from you.

Zego, leading the AI evolution in insurance.

Equal opportunities 🌈

We're an equal opportunity employer and we value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status.

title: Product Engineer (Backend)
description:
Hey! We're team Granola 👋

We're building a category-defining product, backed by a $125M Series C and used daily by teams at companies like Cursor, Vanta, and Linear. We started by making meeting notes better. Now we're turning every conversation a company has into context that people and agents can act on: shared team workspaces, APIs and integrations, and agentic workflows that do something with what was said.

If you haven't already, you should check out what we're building, and why you should work here.

The role

You'll own the systems that make Granola fast, accurate and trustworthy for the next 100x of users, and you'll help decide what's worth building. Our backend engineers talk to users and ship product, not just services.

What you'll work on

  • The voice pipeline. Scale real-time transcription so notes land accurately in seconds, on every device people use.

  • New models in production. Evaluate new voice and transcription models as they're released, and get the best ones into users' hands.

  • The agent harness. Build the harness Granola's agents run in: long-running jobs, tool calls, retries, and retrieving the right context.

  • APIs and integrations. Extend the APIs and integrations that let people bring Granola context into the AI tools they already use.

  • Enterprise-grade trust. Build the permissions, data isolation and admin controls that let a company roll Granola out across every team.

  • Data at scale. Own Postgres performance, observability and alerting as usage grows.

How we work

  • People and product first. We hire people who are kind, down to earth and pragmatic, who care deeply about the product, and who want to stay connected to the customers using it. Product isn't one team's job here; it's everyone's.

  • High autonomy. Engineers spot opportunities and ship improvements themselves. We’d rather you ship it than write about it.

  • Everyone talks to users. Every engineer works directly with the people using Granola, and that's where most of our best ideas come from.

  • A high bar for engineering and product. We expect strong technical ability and strong product sense. Engineers think like PMs: they understand the user's problem and help shape the direction of what they build.

  • Room to experiment. Every engineer has a budget from day one to use new models, tools and technologies which make them more productive.

  • Design and quality matter. Thoughtful design, a high quality bar and close collaboration on everything we build.

  • We work in person, with flexibility. We’re in the office five days a week because we genuinely like building together. It’s relaxed: dress down, bring your dog, and no fixed office hours.

What that looks like in practice: the version of Granola we use internally goes far beyond the public app. We're building at the frontier of agentic software, and we try every new capability on ourselves first.

The team

The Granola team is kind, curious and design-obsessed. Many of us are former founders, others have built products at Figma, Apple, Google and Meta, and we're all still learning from each other.

Who we're looking for

We don't set a minimum number of years. Some of our strongest engineers graduated two years ago; others have run their own companies. We care about what you've built and how you think about it.

  • You've owned backend systems in production that real users depended on, and you can talk through the trade-offs you made.

  • You're strong in TypeScript and Node.js.

  • You know relational databases deeply (we use Postgres): query plans, indexing, and migrations without downtime.

  • You're comfortable with cloud infrastructure as code (we use AWS, Terraform and a lot of Lambda).

  • You think about security and failure modes before the happy path.

  • You have product sense: you can explain why a system matters to the person using it, and you'd rather ship what users need this week than the perfect version next quarter.

Bonus: experience with speech or audio pipelines, LLM infrastructure, evals, or streaming systems.

Our stack

TypeScript, Node.js, Postgres, AWS (with plenty of Lambda), Terraform, plus whichever new models and tools prove themselves. You don't need experience with everything, but you should be excited to work close to the product and at real scale.

How we hire

Our interviews start with the product: who the user is, what problem matters and what you'd build first. Throughout, we're looking for product sense, good judgement on trade-offs, real engineering depth, and how you'd use your experience to shape a product from the ground up. We also look for people who ship quickly, iterate and love to experiment, and who stay kind and pragmatic along the way.

What we offer

We're living in the most exciting time for tool builders since Engelbart's demo in 1968, and we want to build that future together in London. We pay slightly above market on salary and above market on equity. We work together in person five days a week at our office in Old Street, and we offer relocation support if you're moving to London.

Great people come from all kinds of backgrounds. If this speaks to you, whether or not you look like a fit on paper, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Senior HW Engineer – Signal and Power Integrity
description:
The Opportunity

Every board Lumai builds has to run multi-gigabit links and feed high-current ASIC and FPGA rails. Getting those right before the board is fabricated is the difference between a working system and a respin cycle. This role owns the modelling, the stackups, the materials and the design rules that make it work, and has a direct say in the decisions that prevent the respin.

The Role

You will own signal and power integrity across our boards and packages. That means pre-layout channel studies that set routing topologies, stackups, materials and constraints; post-layout analysis of critical channels, including insertion and return loss, crosstalk, and eye and COM analysis with IBIS-AMI models; optimisation of vias, breakouts, connector launches and the transitions into our optical engines; and PDN impedance targets, decoupling strategies and DC drop analysis for high-current rails.

What is genuinely hard is that the channels cross boundaries - chip, package, interposer, board and optical engine - and a model is only as good as its weakest corner. You will spend as much time at the bench as in the tool, correlating what you predicted against what the hardware does, and feeding that back into design rules.

By month six, you will have signed off the critical channels on at least one board, built the model libraries and design guidelines the team reuses, and be the person whose analysis decides when a layout is ready to release.

What You'll Do

  • Run pre-layout channel studies to set routing topologies, stackups, materials and design constraints for high-speed interfaces.

  • Carry out post-layout SI analysis of critical channels: insertion and return loss, crosstalk, and eye and COM analysis using IBIS-AMI models.

  • Design and optimise vias, breakouts, connector launches, and the transitions into optical engines and co-packaged components.

  • Set PDN impedance targets, design decoupling strategies, and run DC drop and AC PDN analysis for high-current ASIC and FPGA rails.

  • Support package, interposer and board co-simulation with the ASIC team to keep channel and power integrity sound end to end.

  • Correlate simulation with lab measurements using TDRs, VNAs and oscilloscopes, and feed the results back into models and design rules.

  • Evaluate and characterise PCB materials, connectors and cable assemblies with suppliers and fabricators.

  • Build up our SI/PI methodology, model libraries and design guidelines so they can be reused across projects.

What We're Looking For

Must-have

  • A degree in electronic engineering, physics or a related discipline, plus proven SI/PI experience on high-speed PCB and/or package designs.

  • Proficiency with at least one major EM and circuit simulation suite, such as Ansys HFSS/SIwave, Keysight ADS or Cadence Sigrity/Clarity.

  • Strong understanding of transmission line theory, S-parameters, crosstalk, loss mechanisms and channel compliance metrics such as eye diagrams and COM.

  • Experience with IBIS and IBIS-AMI models for SerDes and memory interface simulation.

  • Solid knowledge of PDN design, including impedance targeting, decoupling optimisation and DC IR drop analysis.

Strong preference for

  • Hands-on measurement with VNAs, TDRs and high-speed oscilloscopes, and the ability to correlate measurements with simulation.

  • 56G/112G PAM4 channels, or PCIe Gen5/6 compliance.

  • Package and interposer co-simulation, including chip-package-board analysis.

  • Low-loss PCB materials and fabrication tolerances and their effect on high-speed performance.

  • Scripting (Python, MATLAB) to automate simulation and post-processing.

About Lumai

Lumai is the optical compute company building the next generation of AI infrastructure. Spun out of optics research at the University of Oxford in 2021, we compute with light instead of electrons. Our 3D optical technology carries out the matrix multiplications at the heart of AI inside beams of light travelling through free space, which lets it go beyond the limits of both silicon GPUs and integrated photonics.

In April 2026 we launched Iris Nova, the world's first optical computing system to run billion-parameter large language models in real time, using up to 90% less energy than conventional GPU-based systems. Iris Nova, the first server in the family, is now available for evaluation by hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises and research institutions. Aura and Tetra will follow.

Our work won the Falling Walls Award for Science Breakthrough of the Year 2025 and 'Best Overall Technology' at the OCP Future Technologies Symposium. We are headquartered in Oxford.

Why Lumai

You'll work on a new kind of computer. Optical computing for AI has been promised for decades. We have a working system running real models, and the hard part left is taking it to volume.

Your work ships. We are moving from first product to volume production, so what you build this year goes into the servers our customers run.

You'll work across disciplines. Optical engineers, machine learning researchers, and hardware and software engineers solve problems together. You will learn things that don't appear on your job description.

The work matters beyond Lumai. AI's appetite for energy is one of the defining constraints of the next decade. Our mission is sustainable intelligence at global scale: AI that is faster, cheaper to run and far less power-hungry.

You'll join early. You'll have a real say in how we build the product, the team and the way we work.

title: Senior HW Engineer – PCB Analog Design
description:
The Opportunity

At the centre of an optical computer sits a set of circuits that have to read, drive and hold steady some very small, very fast signals: photodetector front ends, laser and modulator drives, precision converter interfaces, and the quiet power and references underneath them. This role owns them, at board level, from the optical requirement through to the production build.

The Role

You will design the board-level analog and mixed-signal circuits that connect our electronics to light, and take them the whole way: specification, simulation, layout guidance, lab bring-up, characterisation and production. You will agree the optical requirements - optical power budgets, bandwidth, noise, linearity - with the photonics and system teams, and turn them into analog architectures and circuit specifications.

What is genuinely hard about it is working at the boundary between optics, mixed-signal and high-speed digital, where noise budgets are tight and the measurement is as demanding as the design. A microvolt-level front end does not care that the same board carries high-current switching rails; getting both right on one stackup is the job.

By month six, you will have characterised at least one full analog subsystem on the bench, correlated it with simulation across corners, and put the layout constraints and test procedures in place that other engineers can follow.

  • Design board-level analog and mixed-signal circuits: photodiode front ends, TIAs, ADC/DAC driver and reconstruction stages, laser drivers, modulator drivers and bias networks.

  • Translate photonic system requirements into analog specifications and architectures with the photonics and system teams.

  • Design low-noise power delivery for sensitive circuits: LDO post-regulation, filtering, precision voltage and current references, grounding and partitioning schemes.

  • Design control loops and precision circuits for photonic components: TEC and temperature control, laser current control, monitor photodiode readout and heater drivers.

  • Run circuit simulation and analysis (SPICE, noise, stability, worst-case, Monte Carlo) and confirm designs meet performance across corners.

  • A degree in electronic engineering or a related discipline, plus extensive experience designing analog and mixed-signal circuits at board level for products that reached production.

  • Strong analog fundamentals covering op-amp and amplifier design, feedback and stability, noise analysis, filtering and precision circuit design.

  • Bench characterisation with oscilloscopes, spectrum and network analysers and precision source-measure equipment, and low-noise measurement technique.

description:
ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE

Au sein du Département Automatique, Productique et Informatique, le poste sera associé à l’équipe TASC (Théorie, Algorithmes et Systèmes en Contraintes ) dont les thématiques de recherche s’articulent autour de la programmation par contraintes, de la théorie aux applications en passant par l’hybridation. Dans ce cadre, le poste a pour objectif de venir en soutien au développement du solveur de contraintes choco-solver (http://choco-solver.org) maintenu par l’équipe TASC.

 

MISSIONS

Sous la responsabilité fonctionnelle du responsable du projet et développeur principal de la plateforme Choco-solver et en collaboration avec les membres de l’équipe TASC, les missions principales du poste sont :

  1.   Adapter l’algorithme bimodal aux contraintes reposant sur des parcours en profondeur, telles que GlobalCardinality, StableKeysort ou Circuit ;

  2.   Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes (p. ex. le moteur de propagation) ;

  3.   Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (lazy) dans les contraintes Sum et AllDifferent, entre autres ;

  4.   Participer à la rédaction d’articles scientifiques liés à ces sujets.

 

 ACTIVITÉS : Activité par mission

 

  1.      Adapter l’algorithme bimodal aux contraintes reposant sur des parcours en profondeur

·       Analyse les algorithmes de filtrage de GlobalCardinality, StableKeysort et Circuit disponibles dans choco-solver et identifie les parcours en profondeur (composantes fortement connexes, chemins alternants, etc.) susceptibles de bénéficier de l’approche bimodale

·       Conçoit et implémente en Java les variantes bimodales de ces algorithmes, en garantissant le niveau de cohérence attendu

·     Vérifie la correction des implémentations par des tests unitaires et des tests aléatoires comparant les résultats avec les propagateurs existants

·       Mesure les gains obtenus (temps de filtrage, passage à l’échelle) sur des jeux d’instances de référence (XCSP3, MiniZinc Challenge)

·       Intègre les développements validés dans la version publique de choco-solver (revue de code, documentation, intégration continue)

 

2.      Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes

·       Étudie le fonctionnement interne de choco-solver (moteur de propagation, ordonnancement des propagateurs, gestion des événements) afin d’identifier les mécanismes pouvant tirer parti d’une stratégie bimodale

·       Propose et prototype une ou plusieurs adaptations, par exemple un basculement dynamique entre modes de propagation

·       Évalue expérimentalement ces prototypes et analyse les compromis entre coût et bénéfice

 

3.      Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (

·       Implémente ou étend la génération paresseuse d’explications pour les contraintes Sum, AllDifferent et d’autres contraintes globales

·       Compare les explications paresseuses aux explications calculées pendant la propagation (taille des clauses apprises, temps de résolution, nombre de nœuds explorés)

·       Conçoit et conduit un protocole expérimental reproductible, puis analyse et synthétise les résultats

 

4.      Participer à la rédaction d’articles scientifiques liés à ces sujets.

·       Rédige en anglais des articles scientifiques présentant les contributions, en vue de soumissions à des conférences (CP, IJCAI, AAAI, CPAIOR) ou revues (Constraints) internationales

·       Prépare les artefacts expérimentaux associés (code, scripts, données) afin d’assurer la reproductibilité des résultats

·       Présente les travaux en séminaire d’équipe et, le cas échéant, en conférence

title: Alternant·e Growth Marketing Manager | Thiga Academy
description:
Alternance · Paris 9e · Télétravail · rythme d’alternance souhaité 3 semaines entreprise / 1 semaine école 
 
Thiga en 30 secondes : 

Thiga est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en IA et en digital. Nous accompagnons les plus grands groupes et scale-ups françaises : Decathlon, Doctolib, AXA, ManoMano, Mirakl, Disney, Leboncoin et une centaine d'autres. Nous sommes 200, majoritairement à Paris.
Thiga Academy, c'est notre organisme de formation. On y forme les équipes produit (Product Managers, Product Owners, Designers, Product Leaders) et celles qui veulent le devenir : product management, product discovery, leadership produit, et IA appliquée au produit. En inter-entreprise comme en intra, on transmet ce que nos consultants pratiquent chez nos clients tous les jours
 
Pourquoi ce poste : 

L'Academy forme chaque année 2000 professionnels et son offre est solide. Le problème : aujourd'hui, elle ne communique presque pas. Peu de contenu, peu de présence, une notoriété très en dessous de ce que le catalogue mérite.

C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. On cherche quelqu'un pour construire, mesurer et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition de l'Academy à partir de zéro : quels canaux, quels messages, quel funnel, avec quels résultats. Pas pour décorer le catalogue, pour le remplir.


Ce que tu vas faire 🖇

1. Construire et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition, avec le Head of Marketing & Events

  • Structurer le tunnel d'acquisition de bout en bout : quels canaux amènent du trafic, ce qui convertit en lead, ce qui déclenche l'inscription

  • Tester des canaux et des formats en continu (LinkedIn organique et payant, email, SEO, partenariats, salons) et couper vite ce qui ne marche pas

  • Créer et itérer les landing pages du catalogue et des sessions, pensées pour convertir dès le premier jet et retravaillées à partir de la donnée

  • Mettre en place les séquences email dans HubSpot : nurturing, relances, réactivation des contacts dormants, avec un test A/B sur les objets et les CTA

  • Accompagner le lancement des nouvelles formations avec un plan d'acquisition dédié, pas seulement un plan de com

  • Créer les supports nécessaires au tunnel avec Figma (catalogue, plaquettes, brochures) en gardant en tête qu'un support existe pour convertir, pas pour exister

  • Représenter l'Academy sur des salons et événements, avec un objectif de leads qualifiés en sortie, pas juste de présence

    • 2. Mesurer, analyser, arbitrer

    Le nerf du poste. Sans mesure, pas de growth, juste du marketing qui se raconte des histoires.

  • Suivre les KPIs qui comptent à chaque étape du tunnel : trafic, taux de clic, taux de conversion en lead, taux de conversion en inscrit, coût d'acquisition par inscrit, taux de remplissage des sessions

  • Construire les dashboards HubSpot qui donnent une vision claire de ce qui marche, canal par canal, campagne par campagne

  • Identifier où le tunnel fuit et proposer les hypothèses à tester pour colmater

  • Faire remonter les résultats au Head of Marketing & Events pour arbitrer les prochains messages, offres et canaux, avec des chiffres, pas des impressions

    • 3. Faire vivre la marque et la communauté qui nourrissent le funnel

    L'acquisition ne marche pas sans contenu ni preuve sociale. C'est le carburant du tunnel.

  • Poser la ligne éditoriale et la faire vivre : posts LinkedIn, articles, newsletters, formats courts autour du product et de l'IA

  • Animer la relation avec les alumni et la communauté d'apprenants : témoignages, cas concrets, un bouche-à-oreille qu'on peut transformer en canal d'acquisition mesurable

    • L'IA n'est pas une option chez nous, c'est la pierre angulaire de notre façon de travailler, et on attend de toi que tu aies cette fibre. Concrètement, tu t'appuieras sur l'IA à chaque étape : générer et itérer des variantes de copies avec Claude, produire des visuels avec Nano Banana et Figma, des teasers avec HeyGen, ou transformer une transcription Granola en article et en carrousel LinkedIn. C'est ce qui te permet d'avancer vite et de tester dix fois plus d'hypothèses qu'une équipe classique.


    La stack que tu vas pratiquer 🧰

    Le growth marketing moderne, c'est une combinaison d'intuition testée par la donnée, de vitesse d'exécution et de bons outils au bon moment.

  • LLM et agents : Claude (Pro et Code), Gemini

  • Génération visuelle et audio : Nano Banana, Adobe Firefly, ElevenLabs, HeyGen

  • Marketing ops : HubSpot (CRM, marketing hub, workflows), Luma, Phantom Buster

  • Prise de notes et capitalisation : Granola, Notion AI

  • Vibe coding (en bonus, pour les profils qui veulent aller plus loin) : Lovable, Cursor pour bricoler des micro-outils internes

    • Tu n'as pas besoin de tout maîtriser à l'arrivée. On attend une vraie curiosité et l'envie de pratiquer, pas un CV exhaustif.


    Le profil que nous recherchons 🌟

  • Formation : école de commerce ou de communication, en M1 ou M2, idéalement avec une spécialisation marketing, growth ou entrepreneuriat

  • Pratique IA personnelle prouvée : tu as un side project, un compte ChatGPT ou Claude que tu utilises tous les jours, un workflow Make ou n8n que tu as construit, un agent custom, un blog assisté par LLM, un repo GitHub, ou n'importe quoi qui démontre que l'IA est dans ta vie.

  • Réflexe growth : tu penses en funnel avant de penser en campagne, tu formules des hypothèses avant de produire, et tester puis mesurer te vient plus naturellement que produire pour produire

  • Appétence data : Excel ou Google Sheets n'ont pas de secret pour toi, et l'idée de creuser un dashboard pour comprendre pourquoi un taux de conversion a bougé t'intéresse plus qu'elle ne t'ennuie

  • Fibre communication : tu sais écrire pour être lu, tu as déjà animé une page, un compte ou une communauté

  • Rigueur opérationnelle et sens du détail : tu sais qu'une séquence email qui commence par « Bonjour {prénom} », ça fait tâche, et qu'un A/B test mal cadré ne prouve rien

  • Sensibilité business : tu comprends les concepts MQL, CAC, NPS, et tu sais qu'une belle campagne ne vaut rien si elle ne remplit pas les sessions

    • Au-delà des hard skills, on recherche surtout quelqu’un de curieux, volontaire, débrouillard et qui n’a pas peur de proposer des nouvelles idées !


    Ce qu'on offre 🎊

  • Stack IA premium : Claude, Gemini, et accès facilité à tous les outils IA quand ils sont pertinents pour ton travail

  • Encadrement et présence au quotidien de membres de l'équipe marketing pointus sur les sujets growth, événementiel et IA

  • Cadence de suivi : 1-to-1 hebdomadaire avec le Head of Marketing & Events. Fonctionnement quotidien en équipe avec les autres Head of (Content, Design) et le CMO

  • Cadre de travail : bureaux 23 rue Taitbout (Paris 9), équipe marketing de 8 personnes

  • Rémunération : grille légale alternance, transparente dès l'entretien


    • Le process 🎢

    Envoie ton CV, un lien vers un side project ou portfolio (même bricolé). Pas de lettre de motivation.

    En termes de déroulé, tu auras : 

  • Un premier call avec notre Talent Acquisition Manager

  • Un échange avec le Head of Marketing & Event

  • Manage customs and international trade: import/export documentation, classification, country of origin, Incoterms and compliance, in coordination with forwarders and brokers
  • Contribute to the selection and deployment of ERP/MRP and planning tools, reduce reliance on manual spreadsheets and build clear supply chain dashboards
  • Define and track key KPIs (forecast accuracy, plan adherence, supplier and customer OTD/OTIF, inventory turns, shortages, lead times) and drive continuous improvement

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

  • Support Comms in telling Impact's story through PR, coordinating with Comms and, when applicable, a PR agency to keep press windows and partner announcements on track, and helping make sure Impact's international stories get told well as the program expands globally.

  • Partner with Design to keep all video and static collateral on-brand, advocating for a high creative standard and Impact’s lens.

  • Carry a consistent visual and narrative thread across launches, blog content, and ElevenLabs Summit presentations.

  • Draft copy for social and blog content, collaborating with Comms to land a final draft, and with Design on all launch-related visual assets.

  • Manage multiple concurrent launches, shoots, and events at once.

  • Comfortable traveling for shoots and events.

title: Head of Hardware
description:
Accelerating embodied AGI.

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Head of Hardware, you own that hardware end to end: electrical, firmware, and the mechanical integration that holds it together, from the first schematic to devices running on factory floors.

You lead the team that builds it. Today that is about six engineers on robotics, three on EMG sensing, and three on camera systems, plus contractors, and it will grow quickly. Our Electrical Engineer and Embedded Engineer roles report to you. You set the architecture they build against, and you still build alongside them.

This is a founder-shaped role, not a management seat. We are looking for someone who has carried a product from a blank page to customers with real skin in the game, wants to build both the thing and the team that builds it, and would rather design than review. If that sounds like you, you will want to do it again at the earliest stage.

  • Run two calendars as one system: Protect focus time, balance competing priorities across time zones, and decide what deserves a meeting and what can be an email.

  • Make recurring admin disappear: Automate repeated processes so they mostly run themselves.

Requirements

The best people we've hired didn't match a checklist. Below is a list of what matters most for this role. If you bring most of it and are curious about the rest, we'd love to hear from you:

  • 4+ years supporting senior executives, ideally more than one at a time

  • You spot the next problem before anyone asks and fix it

  • Experience handling personal admin alongside the professional side, with the discretion that comes with it

  • Organised and dependable without needing a rigid structure; at a ~90-person company you'll often build the process yourself

  • At home in Google Workspace and quick to pick up new software tools

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up environment

  • Familiarity with Swiss administrative procedures (permits, insurance, tax paperwork, relocations)

We operate in an agile, hands-on environment where open engineering and cross-disciplinary innovation drive everything we build.

As a Senior AI & Flight Dynamics Integration Engineer, you will own and develop an AI-driven autonomous aircraft design and optimization workflow at STARK. Your mission is to automate complex engineering decision-making loops and deliver highly performant, software-defined flight platforms.

  • Collaborate with systems and software teams to validate dynamic models against simulation and flight test data.

  • Minimum 5+ years of relevant professional experience in engineering automation, aerodynamics, or flight systems.

  • Strong background in Flight Dynamics, Aerodynamics, and Stability & Control.
